title: Restore authorized Case Timeline filter/page context after opening synthetic source HTML
goal: Complete CAP-INV-110 §12/§17 read-only navigation with an explicit server-validated return link preserving the previously authorized Timeline Case, filters and page. Retain independent owner authorization; preserve original source JSON and source HTML safe presentation.
invariants: Source entry is always independently Case/Entry/source-owner authorized on each GET; a return link is not a permission, sourceRef, principal, tenant or delegated ownership.

Return target must be relative same-origin exactly /case-timeline with identical selected Case and only previously validated limit/offset/kind/q/from/to; reject unknown/duplicate keys, invalid ranges, scheme, authority, fragment and encoded/dot path anomalies.
HTML carries a bounded, per-link server-normalized return URL; no credential or object-source reference in URL, no open redirect.
Original JSON source preview schema remains unchanged (navigation-only field has json:"-"); existing source HTML without return_to still links to default Case Timeline.
Current feature is only a synthetic local browser Journey, not production IAM or a Class-2 source/correction/Case mutation.
security_properties: Fail closed before any source contents are returned on forged cross-Case return context, arbitrary URL/origin/path, duplicate query, invalid page/filters, unexpected source parameters.
No disclosure of denied source preview across HTML and JSON under new return context; a permitted return link invokes GET /case-timeline and re-evaluates Case and typed-source ACL independently.
Fixed CSP/no-store/nosniff/no-referrer retained, all strings html/template escaped.

migration.rationale: Add optional inert navigation query parameter on existing fixed GET route, no changes in persisted objects or source JSON.

rollback.strategy: Revert child navigation context while leaving #205 authorized HTML source unchanged; old unfiltered return and native Back remain available.
verification: JSON preview has no new field

inputs: Immutable parent #205 `49d43f7864c84caef38b8d4a6acdf05ed9ab7057` source HTML with fresh typed-source owner checks and local runnable Go HTTP host
Existing validated Timeline selection parser and paginator; no new auth engine
Canonical CAP-INV-110 §17 return to same temporal position
outputs: Existing Timeline HTML source links include precisely validated source-return context for current Case/filters/page.
On source HTML, return link restores same originally authorized Case Timeline selection after fresh independent authorization; legacy no-return request safely resets to Case view.
Real first-party Go httptest through runnable browser and handler-level checks for return context rejection and unchanged JSON.
acceptance_tests: Authorized Incident→Case→Timeline filter/offset→source HTML→return Case restores precise authorized selection, with fresh GET permission check.
Malformed external absolute/protocol-relative/dot/encoded path, foreign Case, unknown tenant/permission, duplicate keys, invalid selection rejected without source disclosure.
Denied principal, wrong Case, hidden Entry source still refused with optional return context.
Legacy two-key source open produces source HTML and JSON unchanged, return defaults to authorized Case Timeline.
Exact SHA platform Go and security Engineering workflows succeed including go test -race and vet.
definition_of_ready: E10-INV-110N-SOURCEHTML IMPLEMENTED with exact GitHub green CI on frozen #205 SHA, upstream DRAFT not merged
OPEN-013 applies to mutations only and Class-0 read/open/return needs no new decision
definition_of_done: Source HTML and fresh Case destination route actually run via Go HTTP fixture with restored filters/page.
Security and negative tests and exact SHA GitHub CI pass without reducing guards.
Review of cross-route navigation risk complete; no false native GitHub APPROVED, production or canonical full acceptance claim.

performance_budget.rationale: Bounded URL canonicalization only (<=2048 chars) on existing fixed in-memory source handler. No new source IO or second access authority.
